canonical_name: Parametrizable priority / round-robin arbiter with priority encoder (Verilog, Alex Forencich, verilog-axi)
lineage: The two-module arbiter used across Forencich's open FPGA IP (AXI, Ethernet, PCIe): a priority encoder plus an arbiter that can be fixed-priority or round-robin, with block-on-acknowledge or block-on-grant policies -- a SMALL DECISION MECHANISM (who gets the bus this cycle) with exposed state (mask, grant, grant_encoded). Rival to the freecores rr-arbiter already in the vault.
version: alexforencich/verilog-axi master rtl/arbiter.v + rtl/priority_encoder.v as fetched 2026-09-12
entry_points: module arbiter #(PORTS, ARB_TYPE_ROUND_ROBIN, ARB_BLOCK, ARB_BLOCK_ACK, ARB_LSB_HIGH_PRIORITY) (request, acknowledge, grant, grant_valid, grant_encoded)

example.command: iverilog -o sim $HARNESS/tb_arbiter.v arbiter.v priority_encoder.v && vvp sim
example.input: all four requesters asserting continuously; then a single requester
example.output: the grant trace per cycle: round-robin rotates 0,1,2,3,...; fixed priority repeats the highest; fairness counts

human_capability_summary.built_to: decide each cycle which of several requesters owns a shared resource, either by fixed priority or in rotation
human_capability_summary.pressure: simultaneous requests for one bus; the fairness/latency trade-off between priority and rotation
human_capability_summary.success_means: exactly one grant per cycle when any request is present; round-robin serves every persistent requester within PORTS cycles

human_failure_condition: starvation of a low-priority requester (fixed mode) or two simultaneous grants
behavioral_entry_point: flip ARB_TYPE_ROUND_ROBIN and ARB_BLOCK parameters in the testbench and compare grant traces under the same request pattern

lineage_relations.note: two arbiter designs for the same decision

nyx_handoff.how_to_run_it: recipe.json (runner docker); python -m techne.fossils.harvest run verilog-arbiter-forencich
nyx_handoff.what_humans_used_it_for: decide each cycle which of several requesters owns a shared resource, either by fixed priority or in rotation
